Vektor Flow 0.4.0

Native visual applications

VKF 0.4.0 adds the compiled Windows visual runtime. A built application embeds its retained scene, the transparent WebView2 overlay, static HTML/CSS assets, and the WebGPU renderer. Application behavior and event handling remain compiled VKF; C++ is restricted to the thin operating-system/WebView2 adapter.

Frames can combine ordinary add(...) scene operations with a separately loaded static HTML document. HTML-named components, recursive id lookup, owner event queues, default frame chrome, dragging, resizing, and prevent_default() use the same retained runtime whether the tree came from VKF or HTML. Authored UI files need no application JavaScript.

Scenes and capture evidence

The release tree contains 20 short, complete 2D and 3D scene examples. They cover line and scatter plots, dense point clouds, vector fields, surfaces, symbolic constraints, lighting, shadows, reflections, transparency, tinted glass, textures, UI controls, selection, animation, and rigid-body geometry.

Each example is paired with a hash-locked full-compositor PNG captured in a hidden Edge session. The material gallery additionally includes renderer-only captures and a playable interaction GIF, proving the HTML/CSS overlay and WebGPU canvas independently and together.

Release and performance evidence

  • The Windows compiler and generated applications require no Python, Node, compiler, assembler, or separate linker at runtime.
  • The release-host link-map gate rejects C++ UI semantic objects, while the PE and module gates reject bundled or loaded non-system runtime libraries.
  • The correctness-gated large-scene study completes all seven applicable GPU lanes and keeps all five comparable ratios strictly below 1.5x.
  • The retained one-million-point cloud study records pacing, GPU completion, cold-start, correctness, and buffer-retention evidence. It is a diagnostic indicator only and deliberately carries no <1.5x release ratchet.
  • The established core, linear-algebra, and symbolic comparisons are rerun by the release workflow with the 0.4.0 compiler before publication.

Compatibility and scope

VKF remains an unsupported experimental language with unstable APIs and syntax. Windows x64 carries the visual runtime in 0.4.0. Linux x64 and macOS Apple Silicon keep their native compiler and scientific-library packages; the Windows WebView2 UI adapter is not advertised on those platforms.
